Article.ArticleTitle: [Test fixture] Smoking cessation and lung cancer risk over time: a meta-analysis

Abstract.AbstractText: Tobacco smoking is the leading preventable cause of lung cancer.
Lung cancer risk decreased progressively with the number of years since quitting smoking. Former smokers had a substantially lower risk of lung cancer than people who continued to smoke.
Quitting smoking at any age is beneficial and lowers the risk of lung cancer compared with continued smoking.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Test fixture] Smoking cessation after a cancer diagnosis and overall survival

Abstract.AbstractText: Patients who stopped smoking after a cancer diagnosis had better overall survival than patients who continued to smoke. Continued smoking during treatment was associated with more treatment complications.
Smoking cessation support should be offered to all patients who smoke at the time of a cancer diagnosis.
